overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common characteristics of Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks such as SPF and DKIM failures, use of recently registered suspicious domains, unrecognized external IP addresses, and requests for sensitive data or payment changes without secondary verification. The inclusion of detailed email headers, SMTP transaction logs, domain registration data, and correlated activity logs (e.g., login events, VPN connections) adds depth and authenticity. The scenarios also realistically incorporate detection methods and MITRE ATT&CK techniques relevant to BEC attacks.
overall_assessment.consistency: The dataset is consistent in structure and schema across all samples, with each entry containing the same key fields such as 'scenario', 'technical_data', 'indicators', 'detection_method', and 'relevant_mitre_techniques'. The technical data fields are uniformly detailed, including email headers, body, SMTP logs, DNS queries, and authentication results. Date and time formats are consistent (ISO 8601 and common email date formats). The indicators and detection methods logically align with the technical data provided. Minor variations in domain names, IP addresses, and timestamps are appropriate and realistic.
suggestions: Include DKIM signatures in some legitimate emails or partial DKIM failures to reflect more nuanced real-world scenarios.
Add examples where secondary verification was successfully performed to contrast with failed or absent verification.
Incorporate some email URL or attachment obfuscation fields with realistic examples to enrich the dataset.
Add more diversity in sender roles and departments beyond executive and finance roles to broaden scenario coverage.
Include some samples with successful SPF/DKIM passes but other indicators of compromise to reflect advanced evasion techniques.
Consider adding more detailed network flow logs (e.g., duration, bytes transferred) for richer analysis.
Add fields for user response or incident resolution status to provide end-to-end incident context.
